statement: A preliminary tally at Micron's Taoyuan and Taichung, Taiwan unions found approximately 80% of employees support strike action over the internal performance-bonus system; no strike has been called and mediation is still pending.
why: Taiwan is described as about 60% of Micron's global production capacity and a core high-bandwidth-memory manufacturing hub, so a credible strike threat there is a risk to memory output that feeds AI accelerators.

impact.mechanism: Labor action at sites carrying most of Micron's capacity would reduce or delay memory output, tightening high-bandwidth-memory supply used in GPU systems.

evidence.excerpt: a preliminary tally found approximately 80% of employees
Taiwan represents approximately 60% of Micron's global production capacity and serves as a core HBM manufacturing hub.

confidence.basis: Single secondary Taiwanese outlet reporting a union's own preliminary tally; no company confirmation and no formal strike vote has occurred.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: magnitude 1 -> 2; sources: TechNews (finance.technews.tw)
